editorial:
No Hard Feelings is a fun, slightly raunchy comedy that leans on Jennifer Lawrence's charm and a surprisingly sweet core. The setup is wild: a woman about to lose her childhood home takes a job to "date" a shy 19-year-old so his parents can push him out of his shell before college. What could have been mean-spirited instead becomes a warm, funny story about two lonely people finding an unexpected connection. Lawrence is hilarious and fearless, and Andrew Barth Feldman holds his own as the awkward Percy, making their odd-couple dynamic genuinely enjoyable to watch.

The movie moves quickly and keeps the laughs coming, though some jokes land harder than others and a few scenes feel a bit forced. Still, the heart of the story carries it through, and the emotional beats feel earned rather than cheesy. If you enjoy comedies with a romantic edge and don't mind some adult humor, this one is a great pick.
endingExplained: In the final act, Percy discovers the arrangement his parents made with Maddie and feels betrayed, leading to a painful falling out. After some time apart, both realize how much they genuinely care about each other. Percy heads off to college more confident and open, while Maddie keeps her home and starts a fresh chapter. They reunite and share a heartfelt moment, ending on a hopeful note that their bond, though unconventional, was real.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves romantic comedies with a bold, grown-up sense of humor.
